statement: There are 20 coins that look the same. One is fake and slightly lighter than the others, which all weigh the same. A two-pan balance with no weights is used, but each pan has room for at most 3 coins. What is the smallest number of weighings that is always enough to find the fake coin?

choices.misconception: I used the usual split into three nearly equal groups, about 7 coins each, but 7 coins do not fit on a pan.
I only ever weighed one coin against one coin, which clears just 2 coins each time.
I weighed 2 coins against 2 each time, which clears only 4 coins per balanced weighing instead of the 6 that fit.
I divided 20 by the 3 coins a pan can hold and rounded up, as if each weighing tested a single panful.

hints: Each weighing has three results: left pan lighter, right pan lighter, or balance.
Work out how many suspects 1 weighing can always handle, then 2, then 3. With w weighings left, each pan group holds at most 3 coins, and the coins off the pans must be manageable in w - 1 weighings.
One weighing can handle at most 3 suspects. Two can handle 3 + 3 + 3 = 9. Three can handle 3 + 3 + 9.

solutions.reliable: Count how many suspects can be handled. With 1 weighing, each of the three results must leave at most one suspect, so at most 3 coins. With more weighings, each pan holds at most 3 coins, and the coins left off must be manageable with one weighing fewer. So 2 weighings handle at most 3 + 3 + 3 = 9 coins, 3 weighings at most 3 + 3 + 9 = 15, and 4 weighings at most 3 + 3 + 15 = 21. Since 20 is more than 15, three weighings are not always enough. Four are: weigh 3 against 3; if a pan is lighter, one more weighing (1 against 1) finds the fake among those 3. If they balance, 14 suspects remain; weigh 3 against 3 again, leaving 3 or 8; then 3 against 3 again, leaving 3 or 2; one last weighing finishes. The transferable idea: count what each number of weighings can handle under the real rules, then build a strategy that uses every weighing fully.

whyOnTest: Weighing puzzles test both halves, a strategy and a reason no faster one exists, and here the small pans change the usual answer.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
